data.name: गोविंद
data.gender_notes: गोविंद is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who brings 'Govinda', or the divine pleasure of Lord Krishna. The name गोविंद carries the meaning “God of Cows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose गोविंद usually hope their child will grow to embody god of cows and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that invokes the presence of Lord Krishna.
data.etymology: गोविंद belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Cows.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of गोविंद total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_sanskrit.name: गोविन्द
in_sanskrit.meaning: God in the form of a cowherd
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: गो (go) - cow, विंद (vind) - to please or attract. Thus, the name Govind means 'God in the form of a cowherd', who attracts and pleases the devotees.

in_hindi.name: गोविंद
in_hindi.meaning: गो (go) - cow, विंद (vind) - प्रसन्न करना (prasanna karana) - to please or attract.
in_hindi.long_meaning: The name Govind in Hindi is derived from the words 'go' meaning 'cow' and 'vind' meaning 'to please or attract'. Thus, the name signifies 'God in the form of a cowherd' who pleases and attracts the devotees.

in_tamil.name: கோவிங்
in_tamil.meaning: கோ (ko) - cow, விங் (venga) - to attract or please.
in_tamil.long_meaning: The Tamil name கோவிங் (Koviṅ) is derived from the words 'ko' meaning 'cow' and 'venga' meaning 'to attract or please'. Thus, the name signifies 'God in the form of a cowherd' who attracts and pleases the devotees.

in_telugu.name: గోబింద్
in_telugu.meaning: గో (go) - cow, వింద్ (vindu) - ప్రసన్నియోదేశ్ (prasanniyōdēśa) - the one who pleases or delights.
in_telugu.long_meaning: The Telugu name గోబింద్ (Govinda) is derived from the words 'go' meaning 'cow' and 'vindu' meaning 'one who pleases or delights'. Thus, the name signifies 'God in the form of a cowherd' who pleases and delights the devotees.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Govinda" holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, often used as a reverential name for Lord Krishna, and portraying him as the rope that draws us to the divine. The name is mentioned numerous times in Hindu scriptures, including the Bhagavad Gita and various Puranas. The importance of the name is reflected in various forms of art, literature, and spirituality expressed through ancient Indian traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name "Govinda" signifies the spiritual connection with the divine through the attainment of inner happiness and joy, symbolically represented by Lord Krishna. In traditional Hindu philosophy, this inner happiness is achieved through the practice of devotion (Bhakti) and self-realization (Atma Jnan). The name serves as a reminder to seek out this divine connection and inner joy, ultimately leading to spiritual growth and salvation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Govind means 'Govinda,' the name of Krishna, signifying the one who gives bliss and delight to the hearts of devotees. It is a reminder of the divine presence in all, guiding and nurturing us towards our spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Govind was an avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu who appeared in the Bhagavat Purana during the 15th century CE. He is depicted as a cowherd and is particularly revered in the Vaishnavite tradition.
historical_references.context: Bhagavat Purana, Avatar of Vishnu, Cowherd, Vaishnavite tradition

historical_references.reference: Govinda III was a Jain monk, the author of the Prabandha-chintamani, a major work of Jain literature. He lived during the 15th or 16th century CE in Gujarat, India.
historical_references.context: Jain monk, Author of Prabandha-chintamani, Gujarat, India

trends: Devotional Music, Yoga and Meditation, Spirituality
modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'गोविंद' (Govind) is popularly used in modern contexts, especially in the realms of devotional music, yoga and meditation, and spirituality. On digital platforms like YouTube, Spotify, and Apple Music, there are numerous tracks and playlists dedicated to 'Govind Bhajans' and 'Govind Mantras' that help listeners connect spiritually and meditate. These platforms have made it easier for people to practice and experience Indian spiritual traditions from the comfort of their homes, contributing to the growing trend of digital spirituality and mindfulness practices.
